analysis:
The PR changes only docs/reference/configuration.md (head lines 393-395). It adds DARKBLOOM_CBV2_PREFILL_CHUNK and DARKBLOOM_CBV2_STEP_TOKENS rows and expands the DARKBLOOM_CBV2_SOLO_PREFILL_STRIPE row. No executable code, trust boundary, key handling, attestation or authorization path is modified in the supplied evidence. The prose describes the following:
- Gemma 4 gets a 2048-token default chunk.
- Bidirectional media blocks keep 512 when the chunk is wider.
- Gemma 4 values are raised to 1120 so a media block fits one chunk.
- Malformed, zero or negative values restore defaults.
- The paged pool sizes windowed rings from max(chunk, stripe), so a larger value raises KV charges.
The documented controls are operator-local environment variables, forwarded to the LaunchAgent per the doc. They are availability and performance tuning, not a bypass of admission, memory checks or attestation.
Threat relevance: T-010 and T-029 (resource availability) and T-041 (prefix-cache posture) are not changed. The doc states the setting does not change prefix caching, encryption or the SEC-035 TTL/crypto posture. The text says larger chunks raise KV charges, and I saw no claim that memory admission is bypassed. An operator can only harm their own provider's availability, which is already within the malicious-provider model.
Unverified contract: the actual behavior in EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift (clamping, the 1120 floor, step-budget validation) is not in the supplied evidence. A mismatch between code and doc would be a documentation-accuracy issue, not a demonstrated security regression. The patch excerpt in the file_changes entry is truncated, but the full patch unit was supplied and reviewed. No threat model update is needed.
